Symptoms range from acute urticaria (most common) to flushing to angioedema to exacerbations of atopic dermatitis. Food allergy is rarely the cause of chronic urticaria or angioedema. Atopic dermatitis Controversy surrounds the role of food allergy in the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis. Studies show that among patients with moderate chronic atopic dermatitis, 35-40% have IgE-mediated food allergy. Food-specific IgE-mediated and cellular mechanisms appear responsible for chronic eczematous inflammation.

diseases.name: Allergic Reaction
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about common signs of an allergic reaction, such as swelling of the eyes and lips, redness, itching, and hives (urticaria). The provided evidence discusses allergic reactions to various triggers including food, latex, and insect stings, with urticaria and angioedema being common manifestations.

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire specifically screens for systemic and severe symptoms like difficulty breathing, wheezing, dizziness, rapid heart rate, and swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat. These are hallmark signs of anaphylaxis, a severe systemic allergic reaction that can be fatal and requires immediate attention.

diseases.name: Urticaria
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire explicitly includes '疑似蕁麻疹' (suspected hives/urticaria) as a description of the reaction. Urticaria is a common clinical manifestation of allergic reactions to foods and other allergens.

diseases.name: Angioedema
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about swelling of the eyes, lips, face, tongue, or throat. This presentation is consistent with angioedema, which is often associated with allergic reactions and urticaria.

diseases.name: Atopic Dermatitis
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about red and itchy skin reactions. While acute urticaria is more common, food allergies can also cause exacerbations of atopic dermatitis, which involves chronic eczematous inflammation.

diseases.name: Insect Sting Reaction
diseases.rationale: The route name includes 'stings' (螯傷). The questionnaire's focus on localized vs. systemic reactions, timing, and progression is relevant for assessing insect sting reactions, which can range from local irritation to severe systemic anaphylaxis.

review_notes.note: The questionnaire screens for symptoms of anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, wheezing, dizziness, swelling of the face/tongue/throat). A systemic allergic reaction can be fatal in as little as 10 minutes. Any patient reporting these symptoms requires immediate medical evaluation.
